facts.fact: Rohan's grey warden pattu is hidden at the bottom of a sack of walnut leaf in Nimmi's storehouse because the patrol seeks a man in grey; he wears Meera's spare brown pattu (with a hole in the hem), too short in the sleeves.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Kiran needling 'the warden wearing my sister's pattu'.

facts.fact: A grain carter allowed up the lower road with turnips told Nimmi that a crown surveyor woman has been kept in the Garh Neshar guest-house since first snow and has measured the yard, saying the north wall is two spans out of true.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Nimmi report the trapped surveyor (Ila) and the source must be plausible.

facts.fact: Rohan concedes three days in Ranu; they leave at first light on the fourth day, with the Fair four days off at chapter start, one day on the road to Garh Neshar for a sound man and a day and a half for Rohan.
facts.why: needed because the beat sets the negotiation, and this keeps to F178's four days remaining.

facts.fact: Meera agrees to walk the seal in beside Rohan to the Fair meadow in daylight, in front of the assembly; Rohan does not promise to forgo the writ at the thaw.
facts.why: needed as her concession in the negotiation.

facts.fact: The hardest cases in Ranu get a second course; Meera says six days would be needed to treat everyone properly, and Nimmi can carry the remaining waves alone after the third day's dusk.
facts.why: needed to explain the chapter title and her reason to stay.

facts.fact: Rohan carries his draft assembly speech, written on the back of one of Nimmi's tally sheets, folded inside his coat beside Dilan's rope end; the blockade line is unwritten.
